findings.text: the ruff-delta figures do not reproduce under an explicit --config measurement — the authored test files measure 2=2 not the cited 1=1, and the generated reckon/_flight_schema.py measures 99->100 not 96->97; the directional claims all hold (no added findings on the authored files, one added finding on the generated schema that is inherent to the generator), only the cited absolute numbers depend on config-resolution mode, so a future reader cannot reproduce the exact figures.

the availability entry's exact key-set assertion is already broken at the base revision — the earlier serving verdict added serving/serving_detail without updating it — and this node's lane_* keys join the growing extra-keys set, so the failure that predates the change stays live at the merged head; the node correctly verified the base reproduction and reported it under follow_ons rather than triaging out of scope, and the repair (adding serving/serving_detail and, once merged, lane_*) belongs to the owner of that file.

justifications.durability: the behaviour is guarded by real tests that exercise the actual flight_report path with real temp files — a fresh document reporting state/headroom/binding, a stale reading stamped 1e6s beyond a 100s shelf life reporting unknown while retaining figure and age, missing and malformed documents reporting unknown with a reason and never raising, and measured-zero headroom asserted distinct from unavailable in both directions — and the regenerated schema artifacts are protected by byte-identity round-trip tests at tests/test_flight.py:126 and :142 that fail on any hand-edit; docked one for the synthetic-only interface, since the published lane-document shape (state/headroom/binding_observed/observed_at/suggested_shelf_life_seconds) is an unobserved assumption, no real lane document has been seen, and the pre-existing key-set assertion that stays red at the merged head is outside the node's fence.
justifications.evidence: the headline claims reproduce independently — 90 passed at the reviewed head c54a82d and 84 passed against a true base-tree archive of 390e6bd (the +6 own tests, 1 in test_flight and 5 in test_backend_availability, adding zero failures), regenerating scripts/regen_flight_schema.py over a head archive producing output byte-identical to both committed artifacts, and the claimed pre-existing sibling failure confirmed failing at base with only serving/serving_detail missing before this node's lane_* keys grew the set further; docked because the cited ruff absolute figures depend on config-resolution mode and the baseline/after suite fields are prose rather than the armed-JSON shape.
justifications.fit: the change follows the established endpoints_document idiom — a declarative host-owned document the availability probe reads, reported beside the serving verdict rather than replacing it, through the same _probe_* seam with a parallel _probe_lane_document, and the new schema slot lands in the LinkML source with regenerated pydantic and JSON-schema artifacts proven byte-identical rather than hand-edited; the lane_* key vocabulary, mechanism-based naming, and the fail-to-unknown-with-reason behaviour all match the plan's §18 intent; docked one for the growing unbounded availability key set and the dual epoch/ISO observation-age acceptance, both tolerable but compounding the fixture-free surface.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the done-when is met exactly and every clause is independently verified: a lane_document path is declared in reckon/schema/flight.yaml with artifacts regenerated and byte-identical (round-trip tests test_flight.py:126,142 pass); availability reports lane state, headroom and binding_observed read from the document; a reading beyond its own suggested_shelf_life_seconds reports unknown while retaining figure and age, asserted with a stamp 1e6s old against a 100s shelf life; absent and malformed documents report unknown with a reason and never raise, asserted for both a missing file and malformed json; measured zero headroom is asserted distinct from unavailable in both directions in one case; and the two fenced test files add no failures against base, with base 84 / after 90 both recorded and reproduced.
justifications.scope_discipline: the node wrote exactly its six declared write paths across two conventional commits (feat 9f3c0f4 touching flight.py and the schema trio, test c54a82d touching the two test files), kept its worktree clean at the committed head, and — encountering a failing test in the out-of-scope tests/test_backend_environment.py — proved it reproduces at the base revision before attributing it, recorded it under follow_ons rather than triaging, and fixed nothing outside the fence.
